change.title: pr-8
change.description: FIX: proper handling of group memberships
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: totalPages is one too high when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 pages for 50 members at limit 50, and 3 for 100. So `showingLast` is false on the real last page, and Next sets offset to `min(50, 50) = 50` (line 33), which loads an empty page that reads "2/2". The same happens after removing the only member on the last page: `findMembers` reloads at the old offset and shows an empty list. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: Adding a user who is already a member raises a 500 and leaves the group partly updated
findings.body: `Group#add` is `self.users.push(user)` (app/models/group.rb:272-274). On a persisted group this inserts the group_users row right away, and the table has a UNIQUE index on (group_id, user_id) (app/models/group_user.rb:18). Adding an existing member therefore raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. Usernames earlier in the list are already committed, and later ones are skipped. Before this change the admin UI went through `usernames=` (group.rb:244-266), which diffs against the current members, so this could not happen. On the client, `addMembers` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:51-60) has no rejection handler, so the admin gets no feedback. Skip users already in `group.users`, and show an error in the client when the request fails.

findings.title: remove_member leaves a stale primary_group_id and probably the user_count counter
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` deletes the join row and nothing else. The path this replaces (`usernames=` followed by `destroy_deletions`, app/models/group.rb:286-292) also ran `User.update_all 'primary_group_id = NULL'` for that user. Without that, a removed user keeps this group as their primary group, so its flair and title still show on their posts. Also, on Rails 4.1.8, `delete` on a has_many :through uses delete_all on the join model, which skips the `counter_cache: "user_count"` declared on GroupUser (group_user.rb:2). That would make `groups.user_count` in the admin group list drift upwards (I did not confirm this in the Rails source). Look up the GroupUser and destroy it, then clear primary_group_id, as `destroy_deletions` does.

findings.title: Public group members page now silently shows only the first 50 members
findings.body: Before, non-automatic groups returned every member. Now the endpoint defaults to `limit` 50, and `group/members.hbs` renders `members` with no pagination controls or count. Neither `group-members.js.es6` nor `models/group.js` gives users a way to load more. On /groups/:name/members, a group with more than 50 members shows only the first 50 by username, with no sign that the list is cut off. Add paging or infinite loading there, or keep returning the full list for that page.

findings.title: Selected usernames survive Add and navigation to another group
findings.body: `usernames` lives on the admin group controller, which is a singleton, and is never cleared (see the TODO). After adding users to group A, an admin who opens group B and clicks Add adds the same users to B. Clear `usernames` once `addMembers` resolves and in the route's `setupController`.

findings.title: Admin member page offset persists on the shared group model
findings.body: `offset` is stored on the Group instance taken from the `adminGroups` list (lines 4-5), which is reused across visits. An admin who leaves group A on page 3 and comes back lands on page 3 again. Reset `offset` to 0 in `setupController` before calling `findMembers()`.

findings.title: Automatic-group specs depend on seeded group id 1 and use the wrong verb
findings.body: The `.update`, `.add_members` and `.remove_member` automatic-group tests hard-code `id`/`group_id: 1` and rely on the seeded `admins` auto group existing. Line 115 also sends `:put` to `remove_member`, whose route is DELETE. Use `Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)` as the `.destroy` spec does, and send `:delete`. No spec covers adding an existing member or the primary_group_id clean-up on removal.

contracts.action: Admin adds members via the Add button
contracts.equivalent_path: Old saveWithUsernames → update_put → Group#usernames= (diffs against current members)
contracts.before_after: The old path computed additions and deletions, so existing members were ignored. The new path calls group.add for every username, with no check that the user is already a member.
contracts.visible_effect: On success, findMembers reloads the list. On failure, nothing visible happens.
contracts.failure_mode: No rejection handler, so a 422 or 500 fails silently. A duplicate member causes RecordNotUnique and a partial add.

contracts.before_after: The old path destroyed each GroupUser and cleared primary_group_id. The new path calls users.delete(user_id) and does neither.
contracts.visible_effect: The list reloads, but the user's primary group flair remains.
contracts.failure_mode: No rejection handler, so a failure is silent.

contracts.equivalent_path: Old findMembers returned the full list for non-automatic groups
contracts.before_after: Members are now stored on the model together with limit, offset and user_count from meta.
contracts.visible_effect: The admin page shows a page counter. The public page shows only the first 50 members, with no controls to see more.
contracts.failure_mode: The fetch is not awaited in setupController. If it fails, the list stays empty and no error is shown.

summary: This PR replaces whole-list group membership editing with paginated listing and separate add and remove endpoints. I found four problems to fix in this PR. (1) The page count is one too high whenever the member count is an exact multiple of the page size, so Next opens an empty page. (2) Adding a user who is already a member hits a unique index and returns a 500, with some of the users already added, and the client shows nothing. (3) remove_member leaves the removed user's primary_group_id pointing at the group, and on Rails 4.1 it probably also skips the user_count counter cache. (4) The public /groups/:name/members page now shows only the first 50 members with no paging. I also have three suggestions (marked consider): the selected usernames are never cleared, the page offset is kept when an admin returns to a group, and the specs depend on seeded group ids.
